newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Jamaica to develop Kingston as cruise destination.
newsitem.headline: Jamaica to develop Kingston as cruise destination.

text.p: A group of local developers said Wednesday it had signed an agreement with the government to spend US$35 million developing Kingston as a cruise ship destination.
Work on the project was set to start in July 1997, for completion in mid-1999.

Pragma Developments, headed by Jamaica's former director of tourism Robert Stephens, plans to upgrade the existing pier and establish tours to nearby cultural and ecological sites, such as the Blue Mountains and Port Royal, the group said.

Virtually all of Jamaica's cruise ship arrivals call at ports on the island's north coast and avoid Kingston, with a population of nearly one million the largest English-speaking city in the Caribbean, which is located on the south coast.

But the development group might have a difficult time attracting visitors to the Jamaican capital. On Oct. 10, the U.S. State Dept. issued a warning to all potential U.S. tourists to avoid Kingston because of the high violent crime rate in the city.
Tourism is Jamaica's largest single foreign exchange earner. The country received some 1.6 million visitors last year, with gross earnings of US$981.5 million.
